reported.title: Drip pulses fire back-to-back instead of every 800 ms
reported.description: The scheduler stores the next due time in a uint8_t (line 10) and compares it with the truncated millis() value now8 (lines 63, 71). The guard `(uint8_t)(now8 - nextDue) < 128 && now8 >= nextDue` is satisfied immediately after a pulse ends because nextDue was set to now8 + 800 which wraps modulo 256, so a new pulse starts right after the 50 ms pulse finishes rather than 800 ms later. Measured evidence shows consecutive `drip` lines only 49-50 ms apart (e.g. 38.622 to 88.802 to 137.955), far below the required 800 ± 120 ms. Expected /^drip$/ every 800 ± 120 ms; 103 of 105 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 705 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Drip solenoid driver on D8; pause button on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Emit a 50 ms HIGH pulse on D8 every 800 ms while pause is released.
- Print the exact line `drip` at the start of each pulse; period must stay 800 ms ±120 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, suppress new pulses and keep D8 LOW.
- Every 1600 ms print `drip n=<count> pause=<0|1>`.
- Stay responsive: complete each pulse without multi-second blocking waits.
